title: Bulk deprovisioning script for a retired add-on

source.note: Adapted from Atlassian's April 2022 post-incident review (deletion script run with the wrong IDs and in permanent-delete mode).

input.objective: Remove the retired 'Insight Legacy' add-on from the ~900 customer sites that still have it installed, before its backend is shut down at the end of the month.
constraints: The add-on's backend will be switched off on the 30th.
Customers must not lose data of other products on their sites.
input.context: The platform has a site-management API `DELETE /sites/{id}/objects?ids=...&mode=mark|permanent` that accepts IDs of any deletable object (sites, products, add-on installations). `mark` soft-deletes with a 14-day restore window; `permanent` purges immediately. Add-on installations and sites both have 24-character IDs of the same format. The product team will send the list of IDs to delete. Recovery of permanently deleted sites requires restoring from backups site by site.
input.proposed_solution: Write a batch job that reads the ID list provided by the product team, calls the deletion API with `mode=permanent` in batches of 30 with a 2 s pause between batches, and logs every response. Permanent mode guarantees the legacy data is really gone before the backend is decommissioned, which also satisfies the data-minimisation policy. We will run it over the weekend to minimise customer impact and have on-call watching error rates.

ground_truth.material_issue: The job deletes whatever IDs it is given: since sites and add-on installations share an ID format and the same endpoint, a wrong list deletes whole customer sites, and permanent mode removes the 14-day undo path. Must validate object types (only add-on installations), use mark mode first, do a dry run and a small canary batch, and keep restore capability until verified.
required_observations: The API cannot distinguish a site ID from an add-on ID; validate object type before deleting
Permanent mode removes the recovery window; use soft delete (mark) first
Dry run / canary batch / verification of the ID list
